answer: Latency triangulation: a rotating set of verifier nodes spread across the globe pings each key at random moments, building an atlas of round-trip times. Keys hosted on one machine show the same fingerprint, as if fishing one lagoon, and share a single payout. To look like distinct agents scattered across the ocean, a farm must rent separate servers in separate regions for every key, so its cost grows linearly with identities while honest agents pay nothing extra.
